title: Proposition 8.8: cotangent-complex criterion for finite presentation to order n
statement_scope: Let f:A -> B be a map of connective E∞-rings and let n>0. Then f is of finite presentation to order n if and only if: (1) the commutative ring π0B is of finite presentation over π0A; and (2) the relative cotangent complex L_{B/A} is perfect to order n as an A-module. Whole proposition, both directions, not split.
difficulty_reason: Rule author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: the proposition establishes an if-and-only-if criterion for finite presentation to order n using the relative cotangent complex, with a filtered-colimit cotangent argument in one direction and an induction over Postnikov truncations in the other (statement and proof page 41). This is a genuine technical criterion above routine API checking but supports the Section 8 development rather than being a standalone H3 construction.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Equivalence between finite presentation to order n and finite presentation of π0B together with perfectness to order n of the relative cotangent complex.
